process_notes.text: The owner requests a variance from the safety codes officer. A variance may be issued by an Administrator or a safety codes officer (Safety Codes Act s.38(1)).

sources.title: Safety Codes Act, RSA 2000 c S-1, s.38(1)

process_notes.text: A Written Notice of Variance Refusal issued by a safety codes officer can be appealed to the Safety Codes Council: the Notice of Appeal Form, a copy of the written notice and the $500 fee within 30 days of service. A refusal issued by an Administrator is not appealable.

For building, fire and plumbing variances, officers document the alternative solution as Division C of the applicable code requires (Section 2.3.1), send a copy of each variance to the Safety Codes Council within 10 days of issuance, and keep the supporting documentation available to an Administrator on request.

sources.title: SCC Information Bulletin IB-2025-11-18, Mandatory Documentation of Variances

process_notes.text: From 1 December 2026 the Orders and Variances Portal is the only accepted way to register variances. Only safety codes officers register, supporting documentation is included at registration, and registration is not Council approval of the variance.

sources.title: SCC Information Bulletin IB-2026-10-01, Orders and Variances Registration Changes

process_notes.text: The authority having jurisdiction is the accredited organisation or the Alberta Safety Codes Authority. Safety codes officers exercise delegated powers on their behalf and are not themselves the authority having jurisdiction.

sources.title: SCC Information Bulletin IB-2026-10-16, Clarifying Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) Under the Safety Codes Act

process_notes.text: Province-wide building variances and interpretations are issued as STANDATA by Municipal Affairs and the Safety Codes Council, and are published through Open Government records. A local office's variance applies to its own site.
